title: The Long Quiet Between Clio Stages
summary: PI clients spend months between Clio stages. See how Lia, Hona's AI case agent, keeps them in treatment and informed, and logs every text to the matter.
body_markdown:
A personal injury matter in Clio moves through stages: intake, treatment, records, demand, negotiation, settlement. The stage list is tidy. The client's experience of it is not.


Most of a case happens between stage changes. In an Insurance Research Council study of auto injury claims published in July 2026, represented claims took a median of about 440 days to close. A client can sit in treatment for months. For most of those days nothing changes in Clio, and from the client's side, nothing seems to be happening at all.


## What the client sees during the quiet


The client does not see your stage list. They see their phone. If it stays quiet, they fill in the blanks themselves:


- **"Did my lawyer forget about me?"** turns into a "where's my case?" call.
- **"I feel better, so I'll skip PT this week"** turns into a gap in treatment.
- **"My new doctor probably doesn't matter"** turns into bills nobody requested.
- **"Nobody calls me back"** turns into a bad review, or a call to another firm.


Each of these is a follow-up problem. Follow-up is what slips when one case manager carries a full caseload.


## Fill the time between stages


Lia, Hona's AI case agent, runs your firm's playbooks in the stretches a stage list cannot see. Her care coordination playbook sends appointment reminders by text and email, follows up after each visit to confirm the client went, picks up new providers and checks in between visits. When your firm turns calling on, she can call a client to schedule an appointment. Drip messages keep the client engaged while a matter sits in one stage, and Lia answers "where's my case?" texts at any hour from your FAQs.


Treatment is where this pays off. In the same study, total payments ran about $2 for every $1 of medical bills. In Lia's beta, appointments Lia tracked to resolution had 86% attendance, against a typical healthcare rate of about 70%.


## Make each stage change count


When a matter does move, Hona turns the move into something the client can see. The nightly sync picks up the new stage, moves the client's case tracker, sends the update you wrote for that stage and starts the playbook for that phase. When a client should hear right away, staff can sync one matter by hand.


## Clio still has the whole story


None of this happens off the record. Every text, Lia's included, is logged to the Clio matter. Notification history and form submissions land as notes, client files arrive as attachments, and mapped form answers update fields on the matter.


The guide walks through each pre-litigation stage in Clio, shows what syncs each way, and lays out setup in seven steps.

## The takeaway


Clio tracks where the matter is. Your client lives in the time between stages. Hona fills that time with follow-up, and logs every word of it back to Clio.
